by the Burkholder--Davis--Gundy inequality \cite[Theorem~3.50]{peszat2007} and obtain with similar computation as in~\eqref{rhoetaestimate} for $\rho - \eta \le 1$

issues.failure_explanation: For a Lévy martingale with jumps, the quadratic variation [M] is random. The deterministic quantity int v e^{-2λ(t-s)}ds is only the predictable compensator <M>, so BDG does not yield E|M|^p ≤ C(<M>)^{p/2} for p>2. For compensated Poisson integrals, E|∫f dÑ|^p ≥ c∫|f|^p ds, which here is ~1/λ, much larger than λ^{-p/2}. Hence E[Z^{p/2}] ≳ (1+λ)^{ρp/2}λ^{-1}a^p. Summability then needs ρ-η ≤ 2/p (as in case (iii)), not ρ-η ≤ 1. Take a sparse spectrum with ℓ b_ℓ = j^{-2} at ℓ=2^j and zero otherwise. Then L ∈ L^p(H^η), the components are independent, and E||X(t)||^p_{H^{η+1}} = ∞, since (∑Z)^{p/2} ≥ ∑Z^{p/2}. So the claim is false, not merely unproved.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict case (ii) for p>2 to ρ-η ≤ 2/p, or to continuous (Gaussian) components. Use a Kunita/Rosenthal-type bound with p-th jump moments. Weaken the first claim of cor:added-1 accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The regularity gain of one full order in L^p, p>2, for non-Gaussian noise is invalid. Consequently the 'twice the strong rate' weak result of cor:added-1 for L in L^p with independent components is unsupported, as is the prose/numerical claim of p-independent weak rates for Poisson noise.
issues.title: BDG applied with deterministic 'quadratic variation' for jump martingales; case (ii) with p>2 and rho-eta<=1 fails
issues.why_classification: No comparable version of the claimed regime survives for jump noise. The regularity range drops from 1 to 2/p, and the advertised doubled weak rate is lost for non-Gaussian noise.

issues.failure_explanation: Applying weakr with ρ=η+1 (or ρ<η+1/m) requires ass:TestFunc, i.e. X(t),X^(κ)(t) ∈ L^{2m}(Ω,H^ρ) uniformly for t∈[0,T]. prop:regul gives this only if X^0 ∈ L^{2m}(Ω,H^ν) with p ≥ 2m. Its bound is also singular as t→0 unless ν ≥ ρ, and at t=0 X(0)=X^0 itself must lie in L^{2m}(Ω,H^ρ). The corollary imposes none of this: X^0 enters only through its L^2(Ω,L^2) norm and p is unrelated to m.
